concerns.text: The plan cites 'ALFWorld (Factual)' from 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/Heaplax/ARMAP-RM-ALFWorld/...' as a source for 'Held-out tasks for evaluation' with 'ground-truth solutions'. This dataset (ARMAP-RM) is a Reward Model training set, not a benchmark suite of held-out planning tasks with ground-truth solutions. Using a reward model dataset as the primary evaluation benchmark for 'accuracy' (SC-001) is a fundamental mismatch; the plan requires a standard ALFWorld test split (e.g., 'alfworld/alfworld' with 'test' split) to measure task success rates against known solutions.

The plan cites 'TextWorld' from 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/juliantcchu/textworld-GPT4/...' for 'Supplementary episodic data'. This dataset contains GPT-4 generated records, not the raw environment trajectories or ground-truth solutions required to construct the (state, action, outcome) tuples for the 'EpisodicMemory' store (FR-002). The plan needs the original TextWorld environment data or a dataset explicitly containing the full trajectory traces to serve as the 'Source of planning trajectories' for memory storage, not just generated records.

The plan assumes 'Dataset streaming' and 'FAISS index built incrementally' will fit within 7GB RAM. However, the plan cites 'ALFWorld' and 'TextWorld' which, when processed into embeddings (state/action/outcome) for 10,000+ episodes, will likely exceed the 7GB limit if the embedding model (e.g., a 70M param transformer) is loaded simultaneously with the FAISS index and the streaming loader. The plan does not cite a specific memory-efficient embedding strategy (e.g., quantized embeddings, smaller embedding model) or a specific batch size that guarantees the 7GB constraint is met with the cited datasets.
